To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a specific subset of GABAergic neurons of the ARC are excited by the neuropeptides orexin/hypocretin, acting on postsynaptic type 2 orexin receptors, and that this excitation is mediated by activation of the sodium-calcium exchanger.
orexin excites a subset of ARC neurons by activating an exchange current.
orexin excites a distinct subset of GABAergic neurons in the ARC by activating the sodium—calcium exchanger.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the orexin/hypocretin system in the control of feeding behavior and energy balance.
the role that neuropeptides play in the control of sleep/wakefulness and appetite.
how the neuropeptides orexin/hypocretin and GABA interact in the hypothalamic control of sleep/wake and feeding behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Orexin activates a sodium-calcium exchanger, and this causes the neurons to depolarize, which increases firing frequency.
Orexin excites a subset of neurons in the arcuate nucleus by activating the Na/Ca-exchanger.
orexins stimulate the firing rate of a subpopulation of GABAergic neurons in the ARC by activating a sodium—calcum exchanger, which may be an important mechanism for orexin-induced feeding.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
orexin activates a subset of GABAergic neurons of the arcuate nucleus by a mechanism that is distinct from the activation of glutamatergic neurons.
orexin excites GABAergic neurons in the arcuate nucleus of the hypothalamis by activating the sodium—calcium exchanger.
orexin stimulates feeding by activating the sodium—calcium exchanger of a subset of GABAergic ARC neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that

orexin can excite a subset of neurons in the arcuate nucleus, which is the main hypothalamic site for controlling food intake and body weight, by activating the sodium—calcium exchanger (NCX) in these neurons.
a specific subpopulation of neurons in the ARC, which express orexin receptors and GABA, is excited by orexin via a sodium—calcum exchange mechanism.
